recipes.why: Twenty-seven rupees a head. It is the Ekadashi dish an Imphal kitchen can make with nothing that grew in the valley, which matters in Lamda when nothing grew here.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯷꯫ ꯇꯝꯄꯥꯛꯇ ꯍꯧꯔꯛꯂꯕ ꯀꯔꯤꯁꯨ ꯌꯥꯑꯣꯗꯅ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯑꯦꯀꯥꯗꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯀꯔꯤꯁꯨ ꯍꯧꯔꯛꯇꯕ ꯂꯝꯗꯗ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨꯑꯣꯏ꯫

start.en: Sago soaks six hours in barely enough water. Start before dawn for a noon meal.
start.l: ꯁꯥꯕꯨꯗꯥꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯈꯣꯡ ꯆꯨꯝꯅ ꯀꯨꯞꯂꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯇꯔꯨꯛ ꯅꯃꯃꯤ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯋꯥꯏꯔꯃꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯅꯣꯡꯃꯥꯏ ꯅꯣꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯍꯧꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A wide 25 L kadai and a soaking tray. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯲꯵ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯃꯅꯕ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯦ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: All year, on every Ekadashi.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯦꯀꯥꯗꯁꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Rajgira Puri
recipes.sub: Amaranth flour rolled between sheets and fried in ghee
recipes.sub_l: ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇ ꯂꯥꯟꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕ ꯔꯥꯖꯒꯤꯔꯥ

method.en: Mashed boiled potato is what binds this dough. Rajgira flour alone has nothing to hold it and the puri falls apart on the way to the kadai.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯄꯨꯅꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯤꯡꯂꯕ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯑꯂꯨ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯤ꯫ ꯔꯥꯖꯒꯤꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯛꯇꯗ ꯄꯨꯅꯁꯤꯅꯕ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯔꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯠꯄꯗ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Roll each one between two greased sheets and never on an open board. Rajgira dough sticks to everything and tears on the lifting.
method.l: ꯄꯨꯔꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯇꯩꯔꯕ ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇ ꯂꯥꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯄꯥꯇꯗ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯔꯥꯖꯒꯤꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇ ꯅꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Keep the ghee below smoking. Rajgira browns in half the time wheat does and a dark puri tastes of burnt flour.
method.l: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯡꯁꯥꯡ ꯊꯣꯛꯇ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯒꯣꯗꯨꯝꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯔꯥꯖꯒꯤꯔꯥꯅ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯨꯛꯅ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯄꯨꯔꯤꯅ ꯆꯥꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯥꯎ ꯄꯤ꯫

method.en: Fry to order in lots of twenty. A rajgira puri is soft within fifteen minutes and cannot be brought back.
method.l: ꯀꯨꯅꯅꯤꯃꯗꯣꯏ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ꯫ ꯔꯥꯖꯒꯤꯔꯥ ꯄꯨꯔꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯇꯔꯥꯃꯉꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯅꯤꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯍꯟꯅ ꯂꯥꯀꯍꯅꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫

recipes.why: Forty-two rupees a head, most of it the ghee, and on a day when oil is not taken there is no honest way to make it cheaper.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯴꯲, ꯃꯔꯨꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕꯅꯤ; ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯂꯧꯗꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯅ ꯁꯥꯕꯒꯤ ꯑꯆꯨꯝꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫

start.en: Potatoes boil and cool the night before. Two hours on the day for three hundred.
start.l: ꯑꯂꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯗ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯆꯥꯃꯊꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A deep kadai and two rolling stations with sheets. Three cooks.
vessel.l: ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯥꯅꯐꯝ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ꯫

season.en: All year, on Ekadashi and on Shivaratri.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯦꯀꯥꯗꯁꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯤꯕꯔꯥꯠꯔꯤꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Vrat ki Kadhi
recipes.sub: Curd thickened with water chestnut flour instead of gram
recipes.sub_l: ꯕꯦꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇ ꯁꯤꯡꯍꯥꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ

method.en: Singhara flour in place of the besan, and it behaves differently. It thickens twice as fast and half as much is needed.
method.l: ꯕꯦꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇ ꯁꯤꯡꯍꯥꯔꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯅꯩ꯫ ꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯑꯅꯤꯔꯛ ꯊꯨꯅ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫

method.en: Whisk the flour into cold curd and get every lump out before any heat. A lump that reaches hot kadhi never breaks up again.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯃꯩ ꯆꯪꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯙꯤꯗ ꯌꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯀ ꯍꯟꯅ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Stir in one direction until it comes to the boil, then leave it. Kadhi splits in the first four minutes or not at all.
method.l: ꯍꯨꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯥꯏꯀꯩ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯌꯦꯡꯉꯨ, ꯑꯗꯨꯒ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯀꯥꯙꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯃꯔꯤꯗ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯏ, ꯅꯠꯔꯒ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯣꯏ꯫

method.en: Rock salt after the boil and not before. Salted curd on the way up splits eight kilos of it before the vessel is warm.
method.l: ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯏꯟꯗꯨꯄ ꯍꯥꯄꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯀꯥꯈꯠꯂꯛꯄ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯅ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯁꯥꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Twenty rupees a head, and it is the only wet dish an Imphal kitchen can put out on Ekadashi. A leaf of sabudana and puri needs one.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯰, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯦꯀꯥꯗꯁꯤꯗ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕꯨꯗꯥꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯔꯤ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯇꯥꯎ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯃ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫

start.en: The curd should be a day old and sour. Set it the morning before. Fifty minutes on the day.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯩꯔꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯌꯨꯛꯇ ꯄꯥꯛꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯵꯰꯫

vessel.en: A 30 L vessel and a tempering pan. One cook who does not leave it.
vessel.l: ꯳꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯣꯗꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ꯫ ꯆꯠꯊꯗꯕ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, on every Ekadashi.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯦꯀꯥꯗꯁꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Makhana Kheer
recipes.sub: Fox nuts roasted in ghee and cooked down in milk
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯒ ꯁꯉ꯭ꯒꯣꯝꯗ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯃꯈꯥꯅꯥ

method.en: Roast the makhana in ghee until it snaps between the fingers. Unroasted, it turns to sponge in the milk and there is nothing to chew.
method.l: ꯃꯈꯥꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ꯫ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯁꯉ꯭ꯒꯣꯃꯗ ꯁꯄꯣꯟꯖꯒꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯅꯕ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯔꯣꯏ꯫

method.en: Break half of it coarse and leave half whole. The broken half thickens the kheer and the whole half is what is eaten.
method.l: ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯈꯤꯔ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯅꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Reduce the milk by a fifth before the makhana goes in. Makhana in milk from cold drinks it up and the kheer never thickens on its own.
method.l: ꯃꯈꯥꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯁꯉ꯭ꯒꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯁꯨꯕ ꯑꯃ ꯍꯨꯃꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯁꯉ꯭ꯒꯣꯃꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯕ ꯃꯈꯥꯅꯥꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯆꯨꯄꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯤꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯥꯅ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Sugar in the last ten minutes only. Added early it stops the makhana softening and it stays rubbery through the vessel.
method.l: ꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯇꯔꯥꯗ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯍꯥꯄꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯊꯨꯅ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯅꯤꯕ ꯂꯦꯞꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇ ꯔꯕꯔꯒꯨꯝꯅ ꯂꯩ꯫

recipes.why: Forty-six rupees a head. Makhana is dear but a kilo and a half does twenty litres, and on a Nirjala Ekadashi it is the only sweet the hall can be given.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯴꯶꯫ ꯃꯈꯥꯅꯥ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯌꯥꯝꯃꯤ ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯱.꯵ꯅ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯲꯰ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯤꯔꯖꯂꯥ ꯑꯦꯀꯥꯗꯁꯤꯗ ꯂꯨꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯃꯆꯤꯟ ꯍꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Nothing soaks. Ninety minutes from a cold stove.
start.l: ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯩꯐꯝꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯹꯰꯫

vessel.en: A heavy 30 L vessel. One cook who does not leave it.
vessel.l: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯳꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯆꯠꯊꯗꯕ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, and on Nirjala Ekadashi above all.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯅꯤꯔꯖꯂꯥ ꯑꯦꯀꯥꯗꯁꯤꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Bora
recipes.sub: Mixed vegetable fritters in gram flour
recipes.sub_l: ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯍꯥꯞꯄ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ

method.en: Mix the besan with a fifth part rice flour. The rice flour is what keeps a bora crisp for the twenty minutes it takes to reach the hall.
method.l: ꯕꯦꯁꯟꯗ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯔ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Whisk to a batter that coats a spoon thickly, then beat air into it by hand for four minutes.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯨꯡꯂꯒ ꯴ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯠꯅ ꯍꯨꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: An unbeaten batter fries dense and heavy, and at this quantity the difference is obvious across a whole hall.
method.l: ꯍꯨꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯣꯡꯏ꯫

method.en: Slice the vegetables thin and dry them on cloth before dipping. Wet vegetables slide out of the batter in the oil.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯥꯛꯅ ꯀꯥꯛꯂꯒ ꯐꯤꯗ ꯀꯪꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Fry at a steady medium heat. Oil too hot browns the besan before the vegetable inside has cooked.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯥꯅ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯗ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Drain on mesh, never in a heap on paper. Bora steaming on each other go soft within minutes.
method.l: ꯖꯥꯂꯤꯗ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯄꯨꯟꯅ ꯊꯝꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Rice flour in the batter and steady oil. Both are about it still being crisp when it reaches the hall.
recipes.why_l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯥ꯫

start.en: Cut the vegetables an hour ahead. Batter fresh.
start.l: ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯀꯥꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: Three deep kadhais. Three cooks.
vessel.l: ꯀꯔꯥꯏ ꯳꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯳꯫

season.en: All year, and made on every rainy afternoon.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯅꯣꯡ ꯆꯨꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Ushoi Bora
recipes.sub: Fermented bamboo shoot fritters
recipes.sub_l: ꯎꯁꯣꯏ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ

method.en: Rinse the soibum twice in cold water and squeeze it out hard. Straight from the jar it is far too sour to fry.
method.l: ꯁꯣꯏꯕꯨꯝ ꯑꯅꯤꯔꯛ ꯆꯦꯛꯂꯒ ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Boil the rinsed shoot ten minutes and squeeze it dry again. This second squeeze is what stops the batter sliding off in the oil.
method.l: ꯆꯦꯛꯂꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯱꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯒ ꯑꯃꯨꯛ ꯍꯟꯅ ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Chop it fine rather than leaving it in strips. Long strips do not hold batter and come out of the kadhai bare.
method.l: ꯄꯥꯛꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯃꯆꯥꯏꯅ ꯀꯥꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Use a thicker batter than for an ordinary bora. Soibum carries moisture even after squeezing.
method.l: ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯕꯣꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Salt lightly and taste the batter first. Soibum is salted in the jar and a heavy hand cannot be taken back.
method.l: ꯊꯨꯝ ꯈꯔꯈꯛꯇ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Fry at a steady medium heat and drain on mesh.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯥꯅ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯗ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯒ ꯖꯥꯂꯤꯗ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: One jar of soibum, opened in September, still frying in June. Squeeze it twice or the batter slides off.
recipes.why_l: ꯁꯣꯏꯕꯨꯝ ꯑꯅꯤꯔꯛ ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Rinse and boil the soibum an hour ahead.
start.l: ꯁꯣꯏꯕꯨꯝ ꯆꯦꯛꯂꯒ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: Three deep kadhais. Three cooks.
vessel.l: ꯀꯔꯥꯏ ꯳꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯳꯫

season.en: All year — soibum keeps a year in its jar.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Mangal Bora
recipes.sub: Ground lentil fritters
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯁꯨꯝꯂꯕ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ

method.en: Soak the split peas four hours and grind them coarse with as little water as the machine will take.
method.l: ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯴ ꯅꯃꯂꯒ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯈꯔꯈꯛꯇꯅ ꯁꯨꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Grind coarse, not smooth. A smooth paste gives a dense fritter; the coarse grind is what makes it light.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯝ ꯉꯥꯛꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯁꯨꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Beat the ground batter hard by hand for five minutes. It should lighten in colour and a spoonful dropped into water should float.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯅ ꯵ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯍꯨꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: That float test is the whole recipe and there is no shortcut to it.
method.l: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯄꯦꯟꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯑꯆꯨꯝꯕ ꯈꯉꯍꯅꯒꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Add the salt only just before frying. Salted early the batter goes slack and will not hold its shape.
method.l: ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Fry at a steady medium heat until deep gold and drain on mesh.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯥꯅ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯗ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯒ ꯖꯥꯂꯤꯗ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: The float test decides it. Five minutes of beating is the difference between light and leaden.
recipes.why_l: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯄꯦꯟꯕꯅ ꯈꯉꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

start.en: Soak the lentils four hours and grind coarse.
start.l: ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯴ ꯅꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A wet grinder and three deep kadhais. Three cooks.
vessel.l: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯟꯗꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯔꯥꯏ ꯳꯫

season.en: All year.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Hangam Bora
recipes.sub: Whole mustard leaves dipped in a thin besan batter and fried
recipes.sub_l: ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯕꯦꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯂꯨꯞꯂꯒ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ

method.en: Take whole leaves with the stalk left on. The stalk is the handle for dipping and it comes off in the mouth without anyone noticing.
method.l: ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯂꯧ꯫ ꯂꯨꯞꯅꯕ ꯄꯥꯏꯐꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯅꯥꯒꯨꯝꯕꯅ ꯈꯉꯗꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯥꯗ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Dry every leaf on a cloth before dipping. A wet leaf slides out of the batter in the oil and fries as a bare leaf.
method.l: ꯂꯨꯞꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯐꯤꯗ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯅꯥꯅ ꯊꯥꯎꯗ ꯃꯆꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯦꯅꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯏ꯫

method.en: A handful of rice flour in the batter is what makes the coat crisp. Besan alone gives a soft skin that goes limp in ten minutes.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯃꯨꯛ ꯑꯃ ꯍꯥꯄꯄꯅ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯔꯨꯛꯇꯤꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯈꯛꯇꯅ ꯃꯅꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯄꯤ, ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯇꯔꯥꯗ ꯃꯅꯤꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Fry in lots of forty and strain the oil between them. Bits that fall off the first lot burn and colour every bora after them.
method.l: ꯃꯔꯤꯐꯨ ꯃꯔꯤꯐꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯛꯇ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯅꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯆꯦꯅꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯃꯆꯦꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯛꯂꯒ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Seventeen rupees a head. Hangam is the cheapest green in the Imphal market from Mera to Lamda and four kilos of it becomes eight hundred bora.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯷꯫ ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯜ ꯀꯦꯊꯦꯂꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯕ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯉꯥꯃꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯔꯤꯅ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯆꯥꯃꯔꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

start.en: Nothing soaks. The batter rests fifteen minutes. Ninety minutes in all.
start.l: ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯇꯔꯥꯃꯉꯥ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯹꯰꯫

vessel.en: A deep kadai and a strainer. Two cooks — one dips, one fries.
vessel.l: ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ — ꯑꯃꯅ ꯂꯨꯞꯄ, ꯑꯃꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯕ꯫

season.en: Mera to Lamda, while the mustard leaf is in the market.
season.l: ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯀꯦꯊꯦꯂꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ, ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫

recipes.name: Mairen Bora
recipes.sub: Pumpkin grated, squeezed dry and fried in a thick batter
recipes.sub_l: ꯀꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯍꯤꯛꯇꯨꯅ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕ ꯃꯥꯏꯔꯦꯟ

method.en: Grate, salt and leave twenty minutes, then squeeze with both hands. Five kilos gives up a litre and it has to come out or the batter will not hold.
method.l: ꯀꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ, ꯑꯗꯨꯒ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯅꯤꯅ ꯍꯤꯀꯎ꯫ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯉꯥꯅ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯑꯃ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ; ꯅꯠꯔꯒ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯄꯥꯏꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: No water at all in the batter. The pumpkin gives up enough after the squeezing and any added is a bora that will not hold together.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯣꯏ꯫ ꯍꯤꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯁꯨ ꯃꯥꯏꯔꯦꯟꯅ ꯃꯔꯥꯡ ꯀꯥꯏꯅ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯅ ꯄꯨꯅꯁꯤꯅꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯕ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: Drop them in with the fingers and not a spoon. A mairen bora should be ragged; a neat ball of it fries raw in the middle.
method.l: ꯆꯃꯆꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥꯅ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯎ꯫ ꯃꯥꯏꯔꯦꯟ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯆꯨꯃꯗꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ; ꯆꯦꯠꯅ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯁꯥꯔꯕꯅ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯏ꯫

method.en: Fry on a medium flame right through. Pumpkin needs longer than a mustard leaf and a hot kadai browns the outside while the inside is still raw.
method.l: ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅ ꯃꯔꯤꯜꯃꯔꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯩꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ꯫ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯃꯅꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯏꯔꯦꯟꯗ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯆꯪꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯅ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯅ ꯂꯩꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯄꯥꯟ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Fifteen rupees a head, and in Mera the mairen is the cheapest thing in a Thoubal market. This is the bora a kitchen can put out in Wakching at no notice at all.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯵, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗ ꯊꯧꯕꯥꯜ ꯀꯦꯊꯦꯂꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯥꯏꯔꯦꯟꯅꯤ꯫ ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡꯗ ꯋꯥꯐꯝ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯄꯤꯗꯅ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Grate and salt twenty minutes ahead for the squeezing. Ninety minutes in all.
start.l: ꯍꯤꯛꯅꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯀꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯨ꯫ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯹꯰꯫

vessel.en: A grater, a colander and a deep kadai. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯀꯣꯛꯅꯕ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯆꯦꯅꯊꯣꯛꯅꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: Mera to Wakching, from the field and then the cold room.
season.l: ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯂꯧꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯀꯥꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Alu Bora
recipes.sub: Potato rounds in a thin besan batter, fried to order
recipes.sub_l: ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯕꯦꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯂꯨꯞꯂꯒ ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯅꯕ ꯑꯂꯨ

method.en: Slice the potato thin and hold the rounds in cold water until the kadai is hot. Cut potato left dry goes black at the edge within twenty minutes.
method.l: ꯑꯂꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯀꯀꯊꯠꯂꯒ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯁꯥꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯑꯂꯨ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇ ꯑꯃꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Dry every round on a cloth before it meets the batter. A wet round slides out of the batter in the oil and fries bare.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯂꯨꯞꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯐꯤꯗ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯊꯥꯎꯗ ꯃꯆꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯦꯅꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯅꯗꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯏ꯫

method.en: A pinch of asafoetida in the batter. In a kitchen with no maroi and no onion it is the only thing standing where they would.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯈꯔ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯨ꯫ ꯃꯔꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯤꯌꯥꯖ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯗ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯃꯐꯃꯗ ꯂꯦꯞꯄ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Fry in lots of forty and strain the oil between them. Bits that fall off the first lot burn and colour every bora after them.
method.l: ꯃꯔꯤꯐꯨ ꯃꯔꯤꯐꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯛꯇ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯅꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯁꯔꯨꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯆꯦꯅꯊꯔꯛꯄ ꯃꯆꯦꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯛꯂꯒ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Seventeen rupees a head. Potato is the one vegetable in an Imphal store room every month of the year, and eight bora with a black tea holds a devotee till the evening prasad.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯷꯫ ꯆꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯗꯤꯄꯣꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯂꯨ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥ ꯑꯃꯨꯕꯒ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯂꯅ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯄ꯭ꯔꯁꯥꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯤꯡꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯦꯞꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

start.en: Nothing soaks. The batter rests fifteen minutes. Ninety minutes in all.
start.l: ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯇꯔꯥꯃꯉꯥ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯹꯰꯫

vessel.en: A deep kadai, a holding pot of cold water and a strainer. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ, ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: All year, and it is the winter counter bora when the greens have gone.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯅꯤꯡꯊꯃꯊꯥꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Thabi Bora
recipes.sub: Lotus stem cut in rounds, dipped and fried till the holes show
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯀꯨꯞ ꯎꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯨꯞꯂꯒ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕ ꯊꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ

method.en: Wash the thabi three times and look at the water. It comes out of the Loktak mud and the mud sits inside the holes where no brush reaches.
method.l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯂꯛ ꯍꯥꯝꯗꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯡꯉꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯂꯣꯛꯇꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯂꯩꯄꯥꯀꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯁ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯌꯧꯗꯕ ꯃꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯂꯩꯄꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯩ꯫

method.en: Cut in rounds a finger thick and boil them once in salted water before dipping. A raw thabi bora is wood in the mouth however long it is fried.
method.l: ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯀꯀꯊꯠꯂꯒ ꯂꯨꯞꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯇꯪ ꯍꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯊꯕꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕꯁꯨ ꯃꯅꯥꯗ ꯎꯒꯨꯝꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Dry every round on a cloth before it meets the batter. Water sitting in the holes throws the oil the moment it goes in.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯂꯨꯞꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯐꯤꯗ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯅ ꯊꯥꯎꯗ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯍꯦꯛ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯀꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: Serve within the hour with a metpa. A thabi bora gone cold is rubber and seven hundred of them come back to the counter.
method.l: ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯦꯠꯄꯒ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯊꯕꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯔꯕꯔꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯃꯔꯤꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯍꯟꯖꯤꯜꯂꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Twenty-three rupees a head. Thabi comes out of Loktak in Wakching at forty rupees a kilo, and of every bora in this book it is the one a devotee names a year later.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯳꯫ ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡꯗ ꯂꯣꯛꯇꯥꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯊꯕꯤ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯴꯰ꯗ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯁꯨ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯤꯡꯕꯅ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯄꯥꯃꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Nothing soaks, but washing and boiling six kilos takes an hour. Two hours in all.
start.l: ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯇꯔꯨꯛ ꯍꯥꯝꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯨꯝꯕꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯧꯏ꯫ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A boiling pot, a deep kadai and a drying cloth. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯍꯨꯝꯅꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ, ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯐꯤ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: Wakching to Lamda, when the Loktak stem is cut.
season.l: ꯂꯣꯛꯇꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯊꯕꯤ ꯀꯛꯄ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ, ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫

recipes.name: Paneer Bora
recipes.sub: Paneer cut thick in a heavy batter, fried to order
recipes.sub_l: ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯗ ꯂꯨꯞꯂꯒ ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯅꯕ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯄꯅꯤꯔ

method.en: Cut the paneer thick, a finger deep. A thin slice cooks to rubber inside the batter before the batter is done.
method.l: ꯄꯅꯤꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯁꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯀꯀꯊꯠꯂꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯔꯕꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Hold the cut paneer in warm salted water until the kadai is hot. Left dry on a tray it hardens at the edges within the hour.
method.l: ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯁꯥꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯄꯅꯤꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯦꯗ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯅꯥꯛꯇ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: The batter is thick here, thicker than for a vegetable bora. Thin batter slides off a wet paneer face and fries as a separate skin.
method.l: ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯄꯅꯤꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯦꯅꯊꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯅꯕ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯏ꯫

method.en: Fry to order and never in advance. A paneer bora is a hot thing for eight minutes and after that it is a cold cube in a jacket.
method.l: ꯋꯥꯍꯪꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡ ꯏꯟꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ, ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯄꯅꯤꯔ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯄꯣꯠꯅꯤ, ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯖꯦꯀꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Forty-three rupees a head, the dearest snack in this book. Paneer comes up the road and it shows in the price, so this is for Ratha Jatra and for a wedding and not for a Tuesday.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯴꯳ — ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯆꯥꯅꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ꯫ ꯄꯅꯤꯔ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯃꯜꯗ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯎꯏ; ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯪ ꯆꯤꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯨꯍꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ, ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫

start.en: Nothing soaks. Cut and hold in warm water. Sixty minutes in all.
start.l: ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫ ꯀꯛꯂꯒ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯶꯰꯫

vessel.en: A deep kadai and a holding pot. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯃꯅꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: All year, and at Ratha Jatra and Yaoshang above all.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯀꯪ ꯆꯤꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯪꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Hawaijar
recipes.sub: Fermented soybean
recipes.sub_l: ꯍꯋꯥꯏꯖꯥꯔ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ

method.en: Hawaijar is fermented soybean and it is the reason this book works. It is indigenous to Manipur and it does the job that fermented fish does elsewhere.
method.l: ꯍꯋꯥꯏꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯉꯥꯔꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯇꯧꯏ꯫

method.en: Soak the soybean overnight and boil it four hours until a bean crushes to paste between the fingers.
method.l: ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯑꯍꯤꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯅꯃꯂꯒ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯴ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Drain thoroughly and cool to just warm — not hot. Wrapped hot it sours instead of fermenting.
method.l: ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯈꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯏꯡꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Wrap in banana leaves and keep in a covered basket in a warm place for three to four days.
method.l: ꯂꯥꯐꯨ ꯃꯅꯥꯗ ꯌꯣꯝꯂꯒ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯐꯃꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯳-꯴ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: It is ready when a sticky white thread pulls between two beans. That thread is the sign the ferment has taken; without it, throw the batch away.
method.l: ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯛꯇ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯂꯤ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯥꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯂꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Unlike axone next door, hawaijar is not smoked and does not keep six months. Use it within three weeks and buy or make it in small quantity.
method.l: ꯍꯋꯥꯏꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃ ꯆꯠꯇꯦ, ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯳ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Three weeks, not six months — this ferment is fresh, unlike the smoked cakes across the border in Nagaland.
recipes.why_l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯳ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯆꯠꯀꯅꯤ, ꯅꯒꯥꯂꯦꯟꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯦꯛꯁꯣꯅ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯨꯝ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫

start.en: A four-day ferment. Plan a week from soaking to use.
start.l: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯴ ꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A large pot, banana leaves and a covered basket. One cook, twenty minutes a day.
vessel.l: ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ, ꯂꯥꯐꯨ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯥꯛꯆꯥ꯫

season.en: Made in the warm months; the ferment is slow in a Manipur winter.
season.l: ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ ꯐꯩ꯫

recipes.name: Soibum
recipes.sub: Fermented bamboo shoot
recipes.sub_l: ꯁꯣꯏꯕꯨꯝ ꯁꯦꯝꯕ

method.en: Peel down to the pale tender core. Anything that resists the knife is too old and will stay woody in the jar.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯅꯧꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Boil the shoots twice in fresh water, twenty minutes each, discarding the water both times.
method.l: ꯎꯁꯣꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯅꯤꯔꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯒ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Raw bamboo shoot is genuinely toxic and it is the boiling and discarding that removes it. This is not a step to shorten.
method.l: ꯑꯅꯧꯕ ꯎꯁꯣꯏ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯍꯤꯛ ꯂꯩ, ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Slice thin, pack tight into the jar, and cover with a brine of one part salt to about seven of water.
method.l: ꯄꯥꯛꯅ ꯀꯥꯛꯂꯒ ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯆꯦꯠꯅ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Weigh the shoots down so they stay under the brine. Any piece above the liquid grows mould and the mould takes the jar.
method.l: ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗ ꯂꯩꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cover with cloth rather than a lid and keep it in the shade three weeks. A sealed jar builds pressure and bursts.
method.l: ꯃꯈꯣꯡꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯐꯤꯅ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Fifteen kilos of a four-month vegetable turned into a year of flavour. Keep it under the brine and it cannot fail.
recipes.why_l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯥꯎ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗ ꯊꯝꯂꯕꯗꯤ꯫

start.en: A three-week ferment. Start in the monsoon and use from September.
start.l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯳ ꯒꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A 20 L glazed jar or a length of green bamboo. One cook, ten minutes a day.
vessel.l: ꯲꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯅꯠꯔꯒ ꯋꯥꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: Made June to August, when the fresh shoots are up.
season.l: ꯖꯨꯟꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯣꯒꯁ꯭ꯠ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Morok Achar
recipes.sub: Umorok preserved in mustard oil
recipes.sub_l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯗ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯎꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ

method.en: Wear gloves or bind the hands in cloth for this entire recipe, and do not rub the eyes for an hour afterwards.
method.l: ꯈꯨꯠꯇ ꯐꯤ ꯌꯦꯠꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯁꯣꯛꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Wipe each chilli dry rather than washing it on the day. A single drop of water in the jar grows mould and takes the batch.
method.l: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯐꯤꯅ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯅ ꯆꯦꯛꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Slit each chilli along one side but leave it whole. Cut through and the seeds come out and the pickle is far hotter than intended.
method.l: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯄꯥꯟ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯀꯥꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Heat the mustard oil to smoking and cool it completely. Raw mustard oil in a pickle stays bitter for months.
method.l: ꯊꯥꯑꯣ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯒ ꯏꯡꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Pack into the jar in layers with the salt, ginger, turmeric and ground mustard, and cover with the cooled oil.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯊꯨꯝ, ꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯒ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯅ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Sun it a fortnight, shaking daily. It is served a chilli at a time on the side of the plate.
method.l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯲ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: A year on the shelf, and it is served one chilli at a time. Handle it with cloth on the hands.
recipes.why_l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃ ꯆꯠꯀꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯃꯝ ꯑꯃꯃꯝ ꯄꯤꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: A two-week cure. Sun it daily.
start.l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯲ ꯒꯤꯅꯤ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A 10 L glass jar and cloth. One cook, gloved.
vessel.l: ꯱꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: August to October, when the chillies ripen.
season.l: ꯑꯣꯒꯁ꯭ꯠꯇꯒꯤ ꯑꯣꯛꯇꯣꯕꯔ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫

recipes.name: Heikru Achar
recipes.sub: Gooseberry steamed whole and set in mustard oil for a year
recipes.sub_l: ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯊꯥꯎꯗ ꯊꯃꯂꯕ ꯍꯩꯀ꯭ꯔꯨ

method.en: Steam them whole for five minutes until the segments part on their own. Boiled in water they go soft and the achar is pulp in a fortnight.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯦꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯅ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯅꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯃꯉꯥ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯤꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯅꯤꯗ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Dry them on a cloth in the shade an hour before the spice goes on. Any water on the fruit takes a month off the life of the jar.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯃꯤꯗ ꯐꯤꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯍꯩꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯖꯥꯔꯒꯤ ꯄꯨꯟꯁꯤꯗꯒꯤ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃ ꯍꯟꯊꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: Roast the fenugreek before it is crushed. Raw methi is what makes an achar bitter three weeks in and nothing takes the bitterness out afterwards.
method.l: ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯨꯝꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ꯫ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯍꯨꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯕ ꯃꯦꯊꯤꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯀꯔꯤꯅꯁꯨ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Heat the mustard oil to smoking and let it go cold before it is poured. Raw mustard oil in a jar turns the achar bitter within a month.
method.l: ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯤꯡꯁꯥꯡ ꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯁꯥꯍꯜꯂꯒ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯇ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯖꯥꯔꯗ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯊꯥꯎꯅ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Sixteen rupees a kilo of achar and it keeps a year. In Hiyangei the heikru comes down from Ukhrul at eighteen rupees a kilo and free off any temple compound with a tree.
recipes.why_l: ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯶, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫ ꯍꯤꯌꯥꯡꯒꯩꯗ ꯍꯩꯀ꯭ꯔꯨ ꯎꯈ꯭ꯔꯨꯂꯗꯒꯤ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯸ꯗ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯎ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯉꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯂꯝꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯦꯝꯅ ꯂꯩ꯫

start.en: Steam, dry an hour, spice and jar in one afternoon. Ready in a week.
start.l: ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯖꯥꯔꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A steamer, a drying cloth and a clay jar. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯍꯨꯝꯅꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ, ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯐꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯩꯄꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Made in Hiyangei and eaten all year.
season.l: ꯍꯤꯌꯥꯡꯒꯩꯗ ꯁꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫

recipes.name: Champra Achar
recipes.sub: Citron cut in wedges and salted down a month before use
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯀꯛꯂꯒ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃ ꯊꯨꯃꯗ ꯊꯃꯂꯕ ꯆꯝꯄ꯭ꯔ

method.en: Cut them and put them in salt alone for a month before any spice goes near them. This is not an achar that can be made on the day it is wanted.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯅꯛꯇ ꯆꯪꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯀꯛꯂꯒ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯈꯛꯇꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫

method.en: Weigh the fruit down under a stone so the brine covers it. Any wedge standing above the brine grows a white skin and has to be thrown.
method.l: ꯊꯨꯝ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯀꯨꯞꯄ ꯉꯃꯅꯕ ꯍꯩ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯅꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯍꯦꯛꯇꯗ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯍꯧꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯂꯪꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: The spices go on cold and never into a hot pan with the fruit. Heat at this stage turns a citron achar bitter and there is no recovering it.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯥꯄꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯍꯩꯒ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏꯗ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯄꯣꯏꯟꯠ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯁꯥꯕꯅ ꯆꯝꯄ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯍꯟꯅ ꯂꯧꯁꯤꯅꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Ten kilos of fruit gives thirteen of achar because the salt draws the juice out. Jar it in that juice and add no water at all.
method.l: ꯊꯨꯃꯅ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯨꯄꯊꯣꯛꯂꯤꯕꯅ ꯍꯩ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯇꯔꯥꯅ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯇꯔꯥꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯃꯛ ꯖꯥꯔꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯣꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Eleven rupees a kilo, the cheapest achar in this book, and it keeps two years. A temple that salts down ten kilos in Poinu has achar till the next Poinu.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯱ — ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯕ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ; ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫ ꯄꯣꯏꯅꯨꯗ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯇꯔꯥ ꯊꯨꯃꯗ ꯊꯃꯂꯕ ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯉꯗ ꯃꯊꯪ ꯄꯣꯏꯅꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯂꯩ꯫

start.en: A month in salt before the spices go on. Planned in Poinu for Lamda.
start.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃ ꯊꯨꯃꯗ꯫ ꯂꯝꯗꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯄꯣꯏꯅꯨꯗ ꯋꯥꯔꯦꯞ ꯂꯧꯏ꯫

vessel.en: A clay jar, a flat stone to weigh it down and a dry ladle. One cook, a month apart.
vessel.l: ꯂꯩꯄꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ, ꯅꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯃꯅꯕ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯅꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯆꯃꯆ꯫ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯈꯨꯠꯊꯥꯡꯗ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Made in Poinu, ready in Wakching, eaten two years.
season.l: ꯄꯣꯏꯅꯨꯗ ꯁꯥꯏ, ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡꯗ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ, ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫

recipes.name: Ushoi Achar
recipes.sub: Bamboo shoot boiled once and set in oil with chilli
recipes.sub_l: ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯇꯪ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯀ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯊꯥꯎꯗ ꯊꯃꯂꯕ ꯎꯁꯣꯏ

method.en: Boil the ushoi once in plain water and throw that water. The first water carries the sourness that would otherwise take the tongue off, and it also carries what makes a jar swell.
method.l: ꯎꯁꯣꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯇꯪ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯪꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯅꯠꯔꯒ ꯂꯩ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯄꯣꯝꯍꯅꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯁꯨ ꯄꯨꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Dry it on a cloth in the sun a full day before the spice goes on. Ushoi jarred wet ferments a second time and the lid comes off by itself.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅ ꯐꯤꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯖꯥꯔꯗ ꯊꯃꯂꯕ ꯎꯁꯣꯏꯅ ꯑꯅꯤꯁꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯥꯅ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Keep the oil above the level of the shoot. Ushoi is the first achar in this list to spoil if any part of it is sitting dry.
method.l: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯎꯁꯣꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯂꯩꯅꯕ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯁꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯃꯍꯦꯛꯇ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯂꯩꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯄꯔꯤꯡ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯁꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯎꯁꯣꯏꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Use a dry ladle every time. One wet spoon and eight kilos of ushoi is a jar of froth by the fourth day.
method.l: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯎꯁꯣꯏ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯃꯔꯤꯗ ꯑꯐꯨꯠꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Twelve rupees a kilo. In Sajibu the shoot comes off the hill for the cutting, and an achar is how eight kilos of it lasts to the next Sajibu.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯲꯫ ꯁꯖꯤꯕꯨꯗ ꯎꯁꯣꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯤꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯀꯛꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯈꯛꯇꯗ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯊꯪ ꯁꯖꯤꯕꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯅꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯆꯥꯔꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Boil, dry a full day in the sun, spice and jar. Two days from the hill to the shelf.
start.l: ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯖꯥꯔꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯆꯤꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯂꯤ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A boiling pot, drying cloths and a clay jar with a dry lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯍꯨꯝꯅꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ, ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯐꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯩꯄꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Made in Sajibu and Kalen, eaten all year.
season.l: ꯁꯖꯤꯕꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯂꯦꯅꯗ ꯁꯥꯏ, ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫

recipes.name: Yongchak Achar
recipes.sub: Tree bean salted down whole and covered in mustard oil
recipes.sub_l: ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯨꯃꯗ ꯊꯃꯂꯒ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯊꯥꯎꯅ ꯀꯨꯞꯄ ꯌꯣꯡꯆꯥꯛ

method.en: Shell them and keep the beans whole. A split yongchak goes to paste in the jar within a fortnight and nine kilos is a brown mass.
method.l: ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯌꯣꯡꯆꯥꯛꯅ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯅꯤꯗ ꯖꯥꯔꯗ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯥꯄꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏ꯫

method.en: Salt them and leave them two days in the sun before any spice goes on. Those two days draw out the water that would otherwise spoil the jar.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯅꯠꯔꯒ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯃꯥꯡꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯨꯄꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Keep the jar outside the kitchen and not on a shelf inside it. Seven kilos of yongchak in oil is smelt through a closed door and it takes over the whole store room.
method.l: ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯒꯤ ꯐꯂꯤꯗ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯊꯥꯎꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯌꯣꯡꯆꯥꯛ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯇꯔꯦꯠꯀꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯣꯅꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯁꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯗꯤꯄꯣ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯄꯥꯏꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: Keep the oil above the level of the bean and use a dry ladle every time. One wet spoon spoils nine kilos.
method.l: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯋꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯂꯩꯅꯕ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯥꯄꯜ ꯃꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Thirty-six rupees a kilo, the dearest achar in this book, and it earns it: eight weeks of yongchak on the tree becomes a jar that puts it on a leaf in Kalen.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯳꯶ — ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯌꯥꯝꯕ ꯑꯆꯥꯔ; ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯆꯥꯅꯩ: ꯄꯥꯝꯕꯤꯗ ꯌꯣꯡꯆꯥꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯀꯥꯂꯦꯅꯗ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯇꯥꯎꯗ ꯊꯃꯍꯜꯂꯤꯕ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

start.en: Two days salted in the sun before the spices go on. A week from the tree to the shelf.
start.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ꯫ ꯄꯥꯝꯕꯤꯗꯒꯤ ꯐꯂꯤ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯃ꯫

vessel.en: A salting tray, a clay jar with a tight lid, and a shelf outside the kitchen. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯅꯕ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯦ, ꯆꯦꯛꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯩꯄꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯗ ꯐꯂꯤ ꯑꯃ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Made in Wakching and Lamda, eaten till the next Wakching.
season.l: ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯝꯗꯗ ꯁꯥꯏ, ꯃꯊꯪ ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫

recipes.name: Singgi Achar
recipes.sub: Ginger cut in matchsticks and set in lemon juice, no oil
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯥꯎ ꯌꯥꯑꯣꯗꯅ, ꯃꯔꯤꯛ ꯃꯔꯤꯛ ꯀꯛꯂꯒ ꯆꯝꯐꯨꯠ ꯃꯍꯤꯗ ꯊꯃꯂꯕ ꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ

method.en: Scrape the skin with a spoon and never peel it with a knife. The layer just under the skin is where the whole smell sits and a knife takes it away.
method.l: ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯃꯆꯅ ꯈꯨꯠꯊꯣꯀꯎ, ꯊꯉꯣꯂꯅ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯂꯣꯏ꯫ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯍꯨꯝꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯄꯨꯅꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯉꯣꯂꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Cut in matchsticks and not rounds. A round of ginger is too much in one mouthful and the jar goes untouched on the counter.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯀꯨꯟꯗꯨꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯃꯔꯤꯛ ꯃꯔꯤꯛ ꯀꯛꯂꯨ꯫ ꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯀꯨꯟꯗꯨꯅ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯃꯔꯥꯡ ꯀꯥꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯁꯣꯛꯇꯅ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫

method.en: No oil and no heat at any point. The lemon juice is the whole preservative and it works only if the jar is dry and the ginger is dry.
method.l: ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯩ ꯆꯪꯗꯦ꯫ ꯆꯝꯐꯨꯠ ꯃꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯤ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯍꯅꯕ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯇꯧꯏ꯫

method.en: Leave it a week in the sun before it goes to the counter. On the day it is made it is only ginger and salt; the week is when it becomes an achar.
method.l: ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯆꯠꯇ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯃ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯁꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ; ꯑꯆꯥꯔ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯄ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯗꯨꯗꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Twenty-two rupees a kilo, and it is the one thing on a heavy Manipuri leaf that will settle a stomach after a chagem pomba. The vaidya asks for it before the cook does.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯲, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯒꯦꯝ ꯄꯣꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯄꯨꯛ ꯅꯨꯡꯉꯥꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯇꯥꯎꯒꯤ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯑꯃꯥꯏꯕꯅ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯍꯥꯏꯖꯩ꯫

start.en: Nothing cooks. Cut, salt and jar in one afternoon, then a week in the sun.
start.l: ꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯀꯛꯂꯒ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯖꯥꯔꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ, ꯑꯗꯨꯒ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯃ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ꯫

vessel.en: A glass or clay jar with a dry lid. One cook for the cutting.
vessel.l: ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯀꯥꯆ ꯅꯠꯔꯒ ꯂꯩꯄꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯖꯥꯔ꯫ ꯀꯛꯅꯕ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Made in Mera and eaten from Hiyangei to Lamda.
season.l: ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗ ꯁꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯌꯥꯡꯒꯩꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯥꯏ꯫

recipes.name: Manipuri Kadhi
recipes.sub: Curd and gram flour kadhi with bay
recipes.sub_l: ꯇꯦꯖꯄꯥꯠ ꯍꯥꯞꯄ ꯀꯥꯙꯤ

method.en: Use curd that is a day old and frankly sour. Fresh curd gives a flat kadhi and no spice will put the sourness back.
method.l: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯍꯧꯈꯤꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Whisk the besan into the curd first with no water at all, until completely smooth. Lumps formed now never come out.
method.l: ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯑꯣꯗꯅ ꯍꯨꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Temper the fenugreek in oil first and let it darken slightly — that bitter note is what makes a kadhi taste like kadhi.
method.l: ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯗ ꯃꯦꯊꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯀꯥꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Add the cumin, bay leaf, dry chilli and a generous amount of asafoetida.
method.l: ꯖꯤꯔꯥ, ꯇꯦꯖꯄꯥꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Pour the curd mixture in and stir continuously in one direction until it comes to a boil. Stop stirring before that and it splits.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯒ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯍꯨꯡꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Simmer forty-five minutes uncovered and finish with coriander. Keep it thinner than a Gujarati kadhi — here it is poured over rice.
method.l: ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯗꯅ ꯴꯵ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: One-direction stirring and forty-five minutes. Both are patience rather than skill.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯍꯨꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯤꯕ꯫

start.en: Sour the curd a day ahead. Start ninety minutes before serving.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A heavy 40 L vessel. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year. A Vaishnava household dish.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Dahi Raita
recipes.sub: Curd with cucumber and roasted cumin
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ

method.en: Grate the cucumber and squeeze the water out in the hand, keeping that water to thin the curd.
method.l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯨꯅ ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Ungrated cucumber keeps releasing water in the bowl and the raita is thin by the time the line reaches the end.
method.l: ꯀꯥꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯕ ꯊꯕꯤꯅ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯂꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Whisk the curd smooth with that liquid and both salts.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯒ ꯂꯣꯏꯅꯅ ꯍꯨꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Taste it cold — chilled curd needs more salt than it seems to.
method.l: ꯏꯡꯅ ꯃꯍꯥꯎ ꯌꯦꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Fold in the cucumber, green chilli and roasted cumin.
method.l: ꯊꯕꯤ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Serve cold and do not hold it more than an hour.
method.l: ꯏꯡꯅ ꯄꯤꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯊꯝꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: The cheapest cooling thing on a summer thali, and squeezing the cucumber is the only technique in it.
recipes.why_l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Make it within an hour of serving.
start.l: ꯄꯤꯅꯕꯒꯤ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯁꯦꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A 30 L bowl. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯳꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, doubled in summer.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Thabi Raita
recipes.sub: Curd with boiled lotus stem
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯊꯕꯤ ꯍꯥꯞꯄ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ

method.en: Thabi comes out of the Loktak beds and arrives packed with mud inside the hollow chambers, which rinsing under a tap will not reach.
method.l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯂꯣꯛꯇꯥꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ, ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯂꯩꯉꯣꯏ ꯂꯩ꯫

method.en: Push a long brush or a cloth strip right through each chamber. Skip this and the raita is gritty and cannot be saved.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯕ꯭ꯔꯁ ꯑꯃ ꯆꯪꯍꯅꯗꯨꯅ ꯆꯦꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Slice into thin rounds and boil ten minutes in salted water until just tender.
method.l: ꯄꯥꯛꯅ ꯀꯥꯛꯂꯒ ꯱꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cool the slices completely before they go into the curd. Warm lotus stem thins the curd and can sour it before the line is halfway through.
method.l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯡꯍꯅꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Whisk the curd smooth with a little water and both salts.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯨꯡꯂꯒ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Fold the lotus stem in with the chilli and roasted cumin and serve cold.
method.l: ꯊꯕꯤ, ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯒ ꯏꯡꯅ ꯄꯤꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: The one raita with a genuine bite to it, and thabi is cheap in the valley all winter.
recipes.why_l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯅꯤꯡꯊꯝ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯏ꯫

start.en: Clean and boil the lotus stem an hour ahead.
start.l: ꯊꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A 30 L bowl and a long brush. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯳꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: October to March, from the Loktak beds.
season.l: ꯑꯣꯛꯇꯣꯕꯔꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯔꯆ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯂꯣꯛꯇꯥꯛꯇꯒꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Kobi Raita
recipes.sub: Cabbage shredded raw into curd with roasted cumin
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕ ꯖꯤꯔꯥꯒ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯣꯕꯤ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯕ

method.en: Shred the kobi fine, to the size of a matchstick. A chopped cabbage in curd is chunks and half the bowl comes back to the counter.
method.l: ꯀꯣꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯤꯛ ꯃꯔꯤꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯆꯥꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯀꯛꯂꯨ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯀꯣꯕꯤꯅ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯆꯤꯅꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯍꯟꯖꯤꯜꯂꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Whisk the curd with the water first and get it smooth before the cabbage goes in. Lumps of curd will not break up once there is anything solid in the vessel.
method.l: ꯀꯣꯕꯤ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯒ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯃꯅꯤꯜꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯀꯔꯤꯒꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯃ ꯆꯪꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Roast the cumin dry and crush it coarse, do not use a powder. A raita is a plain thing and the cumin is the only interest it has.
method.l: ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯒ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ, ꯃꯆꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯔꯣꯏ꯫ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯅꯨꯡꯉꯥꯏꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Mix the kobi in at the counter and not in the kitchen. Cabbage in curd for an hour smells through the hall and the smell is why people leave a raita.
method.l: ꯀꯣꯕꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯗ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯨ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯔꯕ ꯀꯣꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯨꯞꯄꯨ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ ꯊꯥꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Thirteen rupees a head and no fire under it. Kobi keeps ten days in an Imphal store room where a green leaf keeps two, and this takes five kilos of it raw.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯳, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯗ ꯃꯩꯁꯨ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯅꯥꯅ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯕ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯗꯤꯄꯣꯗ ꯀꯣꯕꯤꯅ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯇꯔꯥ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯉꯥ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯂꯧꯏ꯫

start.en: Curd is set the night before. Shred half an hour before the bell.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯗ ꯄꯥꯛꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯒꯪ ꯈꯣꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯀꯛꯂꯨ꯫

vessel.en: A 25 L vessel and a shredding board. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯲꯵ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯛꯅꯕ ꯄꯥꯠ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Mera to Lamda, out of the store room.
season.l: ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯗꯤꯄꯣꯗꯒꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Alu Raita
recipes.sub: Potato boiled, broken by hand and folded into thin curd
recipes.sub_l: ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯈꯨꯠꯅ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯑꯂꯨ

method.en: Boil the potato in the skin and break it by hand. A knife-cut potato in curd keeps its edges and the raita never takes hold of it.
method.l: ꯑꯂꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯈꯨꯠꯅ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯊꯉꯣꯂꯅ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯑꯂꯨꯅ ꯃꯅꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯦꯠꯅ ꯊꯃꯖꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯄꯥꯏꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Let it go completely cold before it meets the curd. Warm potato splits ten kilos of curd before the vessel reaches the counter.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯆꯪꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯑꯂꯨꯅ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯝ ꯌꯧꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯇꯔꯥ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Black salt as well as salt. A potato raita without black salt tastes of nothing and twenty litres comes back half eaten.
method.l: ꯊꯨꯝꯒ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯨꯕꯁꯨ꯫ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯑꯃꯨꯕ ꯌꯥꯑꯣꯗꯕ ꯑꯂꯨ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥꯗ ꯃꯍꯥꯎ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯲꯰ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯆꯥꯔꯒ ꯍꯟꯖꯤꯜꯂꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Keep it shallow and cold. A deep vessel of raita warms from the middle out and sours before the line has passed.
method.l: ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥꯒꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯁꯤꯡ ꯂꯣꯏꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Thirteen rupees a head. Potato is in an Imphal store room every month of the year and this is the raita for a Lamda day when there is nothing fresh to grate.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯳꯫ ꯆꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯗꯤꯄꯣꯗ ꯑꯂꯨ ꯂꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯣꯛꯅꯕ ꯑꯅꯧꯕ ꯀꯔꯤꯁꯨ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯂꯝꯗꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Potatoes boil the night before and go cold. Twenty minutes on the day.
start.l: ꯑꯂꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯗ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ꯫

vessel.en: A boiling pot and a shallow 25 L tray. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯍꯨꯝꯅꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯲꯵ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯦ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, and the winter raita when the tunnels have nothing.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯄꯣꯂꯤꯍꯥꯎꯁꯗ ꯀꯔꯤꯁꯨ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯅꯤꯡꯊꯃꯊꯥꯒꯤ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ꯫

recipes.name: Boondi Raita
recipes.sub: Gram flour drops soaked warm and folded into salted curd
recipes.sub_l: ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯅꯃꯂꯒ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯕꯨꯟꯗꯤ

method.en: Soak the boondi in warm water two minutes and squeeze it between the palms. Dropped hard into curd it stays hard and drinks the raita dry.
method.l: ꯕꯨꯟꯗꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯃꯂꯒ ꯈꯨꯠꯅ ꯍꯤꯀꯎ꯫ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯂꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯨꯄꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: The batter for the boondi is thin, about the run of a dosa batter. A thick batter gives tails on every drop and the tails are felt in the mouth.
method.l: ꯕꯨꯟꯗꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄꯅꯤ, ꯗꯣꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨꯒꯨꯝ꯫ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇ ꯃꯃꯩ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯃꯩ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯥꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯏ꯫

method.en: Hold the perforated ladle a hand above the oil. Held close, the drops join before they land and come out as a sheet.
method.l: ꯃꯀꯨꯞ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯥꯎꯗꯒꯤ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯄꯥꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯅꯛꯅ ꯄꯥꯏꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯆꯦꯠꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯇꯥꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯄꯨꯅꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯃꯒꯨꯝꯅ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Fold it in at the counter. Boondi in curd for half an hour is a bowl of paste and the whole point of it is the give.
method.l: ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯨ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯔꯕ ꯕꯨꯟꯗꯤꯅ ꯃꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯀꯆꯤꯟ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯣꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Eighteen rupees a head. The boondi is fried in a spare hour and kept in a tin, so on a Lamda day when nothing fresh can be grated this is the raita a kitchen reaches for.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯸꯫ ꯕꯨꯟꯗꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯅꯥꯡꯕ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯒ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥꯗ ꯊꯃꯖꯩ, ꯃꯔꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯑꯅꯧꯕ ꯀꯔꯤꯁꯨ ꯀꯣꯛꯅꯕ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯂꯝꯗꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯄꯥꯏꯕ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Boondi can be fried a fortnight ahead and kept in a tin. Twenty minutes on the day.
start.l: ꯕꯨꯟꯗꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯒ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥꯗ ꯊꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ꯫

vessel.en: A deep kadai and a perforated ladle for the boondi; a 25 L vessel for the raita. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯕꯨꯟꯗꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯀꯨꯞ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯆꯃꯆ; ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯲꯵ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: All year, and the winter raita when the store room has nothing to grate.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯤꯄꯣꯗ ꯀꯣꯛꯅꯕ ꯀꯔꯤꯁꯨ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯅꯤꯡꯊꯃꯊꯥꯒꯤ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ꯫

recipes.name: Bora Kadhi
recipes.sub: Gram flour bora dropped into a sour curd kadhi at the counter
recipes.sub_l: ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯙꯤꯗ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯕꯦꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ

method.en: The curd should be a day old and sour. Fresh curd gives a kadhi that tastes of besan and of nothing else, and the sourness is the whole dish.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯩꯔꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯅꯧꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯅ ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯈꯛꯇꯀꯤ ꯃꯍꯥꯎ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯀꯥꯙꯤ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Whisk the besan into cold curd and get every lump out before any heat. A lump that reaches hot kadhi never breaks up again.
method.l: ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯃꯩ ꯆꯪꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯀꯥꯙꯤꯗ ꯌꯧꯔꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯀ ꯍꯟꯅ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Boil it a full forty minutes before the bora go in. A kadhi cooked twenty minutes tastes raw however good the curd was.
method.l: ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯇ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯴꯰ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯀꯥꯙꯤꯅ, ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯀꯌꯥ ꯐꯖꯔꯕꯁꯨ, ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯗꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯥꯎ ꯄꯤ꯫

method.en: Drop the bora in ten minutes before serving and no earlier. An hour in the kadhi and they are paste and the vessel is a besan soup.
method.l: ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯇꯔꯥ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯀꯥꯙꯤꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯕꯦꯁꯅꯒꯤ ꯁꯨꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Twenty-one rupees a head. The plain kadhi in this book is the everyday one; this is the Ratha Jatra version and worth the extra six rupees.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯱꯫ ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯀꯥꯙꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤꯅꯤ; ꯃꯁꯤ ꯀꯪ ꯆꯤꯡꯕꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯒꯠꯂꯕ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯇꯔꯨꯛ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯆꯥꯅꯩ꯫

start.en: The curd should be a day old. Bora are fried while the kadhi boils. Two hours in all.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯩꯔꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯀꯥꯙꯤ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯕꯣꯔꯥ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯏ꯫ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A 30 L vessel, a deep kadai and a tempering pan. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯳꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ, ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯣꯗꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: All year, and at Ratha Jatra and Yaoshang above all.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯀꯪ ꯆꯤꯡꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯥꯎꯁꯪꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Hendru Raita
recipes.sub: Tomato roasted, peeled and broken into thin curd
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯒ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯍꯦꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯨ

method.en: Roast the tomato on the flame and peel it before it goes into the curd. A raw tomato in curd sours nine kilos of it within the hour.
method.l: ꯍꯦꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯩꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯒ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯆꯪꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯗ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯍꯦꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯨꯅ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯥꯄꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: Break it by hand and do not chop it. A knife-cut tomato bleeds and the whole vessel is pink instead of white with red in it.
method.l: ꯈꯨꯠꯅ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯀꯎ, ꯊꯉꯣꯂꯅ ꯀꯛꯂꯣꯏ꯫ ꯊꯉꯣꯂꯅ ꯀꯛꯂꯕ ꯍꯦꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯨꯅ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯆꯦꯅꯊꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯑꯉꯧꯕꯗ ꯑꯉꯥꯡꯕ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯇꯃꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: A pinch of sugar against the chilli and the tomato. It is what a Manipuri kitchen puts in a curd dish and nobody can name it afterwards.
method.l: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯥꯏꯑꯣꯛꯇ ꯆꯤꯅꯤ ꯈꯔ꯫ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯇ ꯍꯥꯄꯄ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯗꯨꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯀꯅꯥꯅꯁꯨ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯍꯥꯌꯕ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Fold it in at the counter and keep it shallow. A deep vessel warms from the middle and a warm tomato raita is thrown, not served.
method.l: ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯁꯥꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯍꯦꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯨ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯂꯪꯊꯣꯛꯀꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Thirteen rupees a head, and it is the raita to make when the cabbage has run out and the cucumber season is over. Tomato is in the Imphal market every month of the year.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯳, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯣꯕꯤ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯨꯝꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯂꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯁꯥꯒꯗꯕ ꯔꯥꯏꯇꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫ ꯆꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯜ ꯀꯦꯊꯦꯂꯗ ꯍꯦꯟꯗ꯭ꯔꯨ ꯂꯩ꯫

start.en: Curd is set the night before. Roast and peel half an hour before the bell.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯗ ꯄꯥꯛꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯒꯪ ꯈꯣꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗꯨꯅ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫

vessel.en: An open flame and a shallow 25 L tray. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯩ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯲꯵ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯦ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, and cheapest in Mera and Hiyangei.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯦꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯌꯥꯡꯒꯩꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯃꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Chak-hao Khichdi
recipes.sub: Black rice and moong dal
recipes.sub_l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ

method.en: Soak the black rice six hours. Chak-hao has its bran on and takes roughly twice as long as white rice to soften.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯶ ꯅꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯁꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cook the rice alone for thirty minutes before the dal goes in. Put in together, the dal is paste before the rice is soft.
method.l: ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯍꯥꯞꯄꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯳꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Use a pressure vessel. Chak-hao in an open pot can take ninety minutes and still be chewy.
method.l: ꯄ꯭ꯔꯦꯁꯔ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Do not throw the purple water away at any point. That colour is the whole dish and it is in the water.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Add the dal, ginger, turmeric and salt and cook a further twenty minutes.
method.l: ꯃꯉꯥꯜ, ꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯒ ꯲꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Temper the cumin, bay leaf and asafoetida in ghee and stir through, then finish with crushed pepper.
method.l: ꯉꯥꯃꯨ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯗ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯒ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: The colour is the point and it comes out of the cooking water. Cook the rice first or the dal is lost.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯃꯔꯨꯑꯣꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ꯫

start.en: Soak the black rice six hours. Start two hours before serving.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯶ ꯅꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A heavy 40 L pressure vessel. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Moong Khichdi
recipes.sub: Rice and moong dal for a light meal
recipes.sub_l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ

method.en: Use more dal and less rice than in an ordinary khichdi. That is what makes this the dish given to someone unwell.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Wash both in three changes of water and soak thirty minutes.
method.l: ꯑꯅꯤꯃꯛ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯂꯛ ꯆꯦꯛꯂꯒ ꯳꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯅꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cook it looser than a normal khichdi — closer to four parts water than three.
method.l: ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤꯗꯒꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Season with black pepper rather than chilli. This is meant to be gentle and chilli defeats the purpose entirely.
method.l: ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯃꯨꯕ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cook covered on a low flame twenty-five minutes, stirring up from the bottom twice.
method.l: ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯗꯨꯅ ꯲꯵ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Temper the cumin, bay leaf and asafoetida in ghee and serve with a well of ghee in each portion.
method.l: ꯉꯥꯃꯨ ꯊꯥꯑꯣ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯒ ꯄꯤꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: The dish to have ready when someone cannot eat what everyone else is eating.
recipes.why_l: ꯅꯥꯕ ꯃꯤꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯦꯝꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ꯫

start.en: Soak rice and dal thirty minutes. Start fifty minutes before serving.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯳꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯅꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A heavy 40 L vessel with a close lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year. The dish for a sick tray.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Sabzi Khichdi
recipes.sub: Khichdi with seasonal vegetables
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯄ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ

method.en: Cut all the vegetables to the same size. Mixed sizes mean the carrot is raw when the beans are collapsing.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯔꯥꯡ ꯆꯥꯅꯅ ꯀꯥꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Temper the cumin, bay leaf and asafoetida in ghee, add the ginger and chilli, then the vegetables and fry four minutes.
method.l: ꯉꯥꯃꯨ ꯊꯥꯑꯣꯗ ꯖꯤꯔꯥ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯤꯡ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯒ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Frying the vegetables first is what keeps them from disappearing. Added straight to the water they go to pulp before the rice is done.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯀꯥꯡꯕꯅ ꯃꯈꯣꯏ ꯃꯥꯡꯍꯅꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Add the soaked grain, hot water, turmeric and salt.
method.l: ꯅꯃꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ, ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯨꯝ ꯍꯥꯞꯆꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cook covered on a low flame twenty-five minutes, stirring up from the bottom twice.
method.l: ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯗꯨꯅ ꯲꯵ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯣꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Finish with coriander and keep hot water aside — it thickens as it stands.
method.l: ꯀꯣꯛꯆꯥꯎ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯒ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: One vessel and whatever the market gave. Frying the vegetables first is the only step with judgement in it.
recipes.why_l: ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃ ꯈꯛꯇ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯐꯪꯕ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ꯫

start.en: Soak rice and dal thirty minutes, cut the vegetables an hour ahead.
start.l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯳꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯅꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A heavy 45 L vessel. Two cooks.

season.en: All year with whatever the market gave.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯐꯪꯕ ꯃꯅꯥꯅ꯫

recipes.name: Hawai Khichdi
recipes.sub: Rice and white soybean cooked soft in one vessel
recipes.sub_l: ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯃꯅꯤꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯑꯉꯧꯕ

method.en: Soak the hawai eight hours and cook it half done before the rice goes in. Started together, the rice is paste while the bean is still a bead.
method.l: ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯅꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯝꯂꯒ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯍꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯧꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯃꯔꯨꯒꯨꯝꯅ ꯂꯩꯉꯩꯗ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Four parts water to one of grain and let it go soft. This is not a pulao; a khichdi with separate grains has failed at what it was for.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯃꯔꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯤꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯍꯨꯃꯍꯅꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯄꯨꯂꯥꯎ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ; ꯆꯥꯛ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯅꯅ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤꯅ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯊꯕꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Rub the soybean skins off after soaking. A hawai skin does not soften and it is felt in every spoon of thirty litres.
method.l: ꯅꯃꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯍꯋꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯍꯋꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯤꯗꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯳꯰ꯒꯤ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯏ꯫

method.en: Raw mustard oil over each plate at the counter. In a Manipuri khichdi that spoon of uncooked oil is what a ghee would be elsewhere.
method.l: ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯇꯥꯎ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯊꯥꯎ꯫ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤꯗ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯃꯐꯃꯗ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕꯅ ꯑꯣꯏꯒꯗꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Twenty-one rupees a head, one vessel and one cook. Two kilos of hawai gives a hundred people the protein of a meal without a second pot on the fire.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯱, ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫ ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯅꯤꯅ ꯃꯩꯗ ꯑꯅꯤꯁꯨꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃ ꯊꯃꯗꯅ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯆꯥꯃꯗ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯄꯤ꯫

start.en: Hawai soaks eight hours. Start the evening before.
start.l: ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯅꯃꯃꯤ꯫ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡꯗ ꯍꯧꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A 40 L vessel with a close lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯆꯦꯛꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, and any day the hall is short of cooks.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯗ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯋꯥꯠꯄ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Hangam Khichdi
recipes.sub: Mustard leaf folded in at the end so the khichdi stays green
recipes.sub_l: ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯂꯩꯅꯕ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ

method.en: Chop the hangam and keep it aside until the khichdi is done. Cooked from the start, four kilos of it turns thirty litres the colour of a wet road.
method.l: ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯛꯂꯒ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯁꯦꯝꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯧꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯔꯤꯅ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯳꯰ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: Fold it in with the fire off and put the lid on four minutes. The heat left in the vessel wilts it and nothing more is needed.
method.l: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯛꯇꯨꯅ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯒ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯀꯨꯞꯄꯨ꯫ ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯋꯥꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯁꯥꯕꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯤꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯀꯔꯤꯁꯨ ꯆꯪꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Half the turmeric a plain khichdi takes and no more. Yellow over green gives a khichdi the colour of old grass.
method.l: ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯌꯥꯏꯡꯒꯪ, ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯑꯁꯪꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤꯗ ꯑꯔꯤꯕ ꯅꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤ꯫

method.en: Serve within the half hour. Hangam in a warm vessel goes from green to grey faster than any other leaf in this book.
method.l: ꯄꯨꯡ ꯃꯈꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯍꯉꯥꯃꯅ ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯊꯨꯅ ꯑꯁꯪꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕꯗ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Twenty rupees a head, and in Lamda the hangam is the cheapest green in the Imphal market. Green on a leaf in that month is worth putting on the menu for its own sake.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯰, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯝꯗꯗ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯜ ꯀꯦꯊꯦꯂꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯕ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯉꯥꯃꯅꯤ꯫ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯇꯥꯎꯗ ꯑꯁꯪꯕ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯃꯗꯃꯛꯇꯁꯨ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯗ ꯊꯃꯖꯅꯤꯡꯉꯥꯏ ꯑꯣꯏ꯫

start.en: Nothing soaks. Forty minutes, and the hangam is chopped while the khichdi cooks.
start.l: ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯴꯰, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯛꯏ꯫

vessel.en: A 40 L vessel with a lid. Two cooks — one for the chopping.
vessel.l: ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ — ꯑꯃꯅ ꯀꯛꯅꯕ꯫

season.en: Mera to Lamda, while the mustard leaf is in the market.
season.l: ꯍꯉꯥꯝ ꯃꯅꯥ ꯀꯦꯊꯦꯂꯗ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ, ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯝꯗ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ꯫

recipes.name: Yendem Khichdi
recipes.sub: Colocasia cooked into the khichdi until it thickens it
recipes.sub_l: ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯃꯗꯨꯗ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯌꯦꯟꯗꯦꯝ

method.en: Boil the yendem in the skin and peel it before it goes in. Peeled raw it itches the hands of whoever is cutting and the itch lasts the afternoon.
method.l: ꯌꯦꯟꯗꯦꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯆꯪꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯄ ꯃꯤ ꯑꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯈꯨꯠ ꯆꯤꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯤꯛꯄ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯗꯥꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫

method.en: Break the yendem by hand into large pieces. A small piece dissolves and thirty-two litres is a grey paste with no pieces in it.
method.l: ꯌꯦꯟꯗꯦꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯈꯨꯠꯅ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯀꯎ꯫ ꯑꯄꯤꯛꯄ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯥꯡꯈꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯳꯲ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏ꯫

method.en: The yendem is what thickens this khichdi and no flour is needed. Five kilos of it in thirty-two litres is the whole measure.
method.l: ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯌꯦꯟꯗꯦꯃꯅꯤ, ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯆꯪꯗꯦ꯫ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯳꯲ꯗ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯉꯥ ꯑꯗꯨꯅꯤ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯕ ꯃꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ꯫

method.en: Keep it looser than a plain khichdi. Yendem drinks for twenty minutes after the fire is out and one that is right in the kitchen is a solid in the hall.
method.l: ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯌꯦꯟꯗꯦꯃꯅ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ ꯆꯨꯄꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯗ ꯆꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯨꯞꯄꯨꯗ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Nineteen rupees a head. Yendem grows behind every Manipuri kitchen and nobody plants it, and five kilos of it takes the place of a kilo of dal.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯹꯫ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯊꯪꯕꯗ ꯌꯦꯟꯗꯦꯝ ꯍꯧꯏ, ꯀꯅꯥꯅꯁꯨ ꯊꯥꯗꯦ; ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯉꯥꯅ ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯃꯦꯅꯖꯩ꯫

start.en: Nothing soaks, but the yendem boils and is peeled first. Ninety minutes in all.
start.l: ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕꯗ ꯌꯦꯟꯗꯦꯝ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯏ꯫ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯹꯰꯫

vessel.en: A boiling pot and a 40 L vessel with a lid. Two cooks.
vessel.l: ꯍꯨꯝꯅꯕ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: Mera to Wakching, out of the ground behind the kitchen.
season.l: ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗꯒꯤ ꯋꯥꯛꯆꯤꯡ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ, ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡ ꯊꯪꯕꯒꯤ ꯂꯩꯃꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Masoor Khichdi
recipes.sub: Whole masoor cooked with rice until the skins split
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯀꯥꯏꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯀ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯨꯔ

method.en: Soak the masoor two hours. The whole lentil has a skin on it and an unsoaked one is still a bead when the rice has gone to paste.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯃꯁꯨꯔꯗ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯂꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗꯁꯨ ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨꯒꯨꯝꯅ ꯂꯩ꯫

method.en: Cook the masoor twenty minutes before the rice goes in. Started together, this is a khichdi with hard lentils and broken rice in the same spoon.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯒꯤ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯃꯁꯨꯔ ꯍꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯧꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯆꯃꯆ ꯑꯃꯗꯃꯛꯇ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯃꯁꯨꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯥꯏꯔꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Only a little Manipuri masala — a hundred and twenty grams in thirty litres. A khichdi is not a thongba and too much masala makes it one.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯈꯔ ꯈꯛꯇ — ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯳꯰ꯗ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯥꯝ ꯱꯲꯰꯫ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯌꯥꯝꯅ ꯍꯥꯄꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Keep it looser than it should be. Masoor drinks for twenty minutes after the fire is out and comes to the counter right.
method.l: ꯆꯨꯝꯒꯗꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯃꯩ ꯃꯨꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯁꯨꯔꯅ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ ꯆꯨꯄꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯦꯟꯊꯣꯛꯐꯃꯗ ꯆꯨꯝꯅ ꯂꯥꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Nineteen rupees a head, and masoor is the cheapest whole pulse in the Imphal market for eight months of the year. It cooks in half the time hawai does.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯹, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯍꯤꯒꯤ ꯊꯥ ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯜ ꯀꯦꯊꯦꯂꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯕ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯍꯋꯥꯏ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯨꯔꯅꯤ꯫ ꯍꯋꯥꯏꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯍꯨꯝꯃꯤ꯫

start.en: Masoor soaks two hours. Three hours before the bell in all.
start.l: ꯃꯁꯨꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯃꯃꯤ꯫ ꯒꯪ ꯈꯣꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ꯫

vessel.en: A 40 L vessel with a lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, and every second day in Lamda.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯝꯗꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Chana Dal Khichdi
recipes.sub: Chana dal soaked long and cooked with rice to hold its shape
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯆꯥꯑꯣꯡ ꯂꯩꯅꯕ ꯀꯨꯏꯅ ꯅꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯆꯥꯛꯀ ꯂꯣꯌꯅꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ

method.en: Soak the chana dal four hours and not two. It is the hardest dal in this store room and a short soak means an hour more on the fire.
method.l: ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯅꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯗꯤꯄꯣ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯀꯅꯕ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯅꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯕ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯋꯥꯠꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯃꯩꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫

method.en: Cook the dal half done before the rice goes in. Started together, the rice is paste when the chana is still a bead.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯍꯥꯄꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯍꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯧꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯆꯅꯥ ꯃꯔꯨꯒꯨꯝꯅ ꯂꯩꯉꯩꯗ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: This is the one khichdi in the book where a whole grain of dal is a good sign. Keep it loose and let the dal be seen.
method.l: ꯂꯥꯏꯔꯤꯛ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯗꯥꯜꯒꯤ ꯑꯄꯨꯟꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯐꯕ ꯈꯨꯗꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯂꯒ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯎꯍꯅꯨ꯫

method.en: Ghee generously at the end. Chana dal is dry in the mouth and without the ghee a devotee stops halfway through the plate.
method.l: ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕ ꯃꯔꯥꯡ ꯀꯥꯏꯅ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯨ꯫ ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯥꯗ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯁꯦꯡꯕ ꯌꯥꯑꯣꯗ꯭ꯔꯕꯗꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯤꯡꯕꯅ ꯇꯥꯎꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏꯗ ꯂꯦꯞꯂꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Twenty-one rupees a head and it holds a devotee longer than any other khichdi here. On the morning of a long walk to a lai haraoba this is what the kitchen sends out.
recipes.why_l: ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯱, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄ ꯈꯤꯆꯗꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯤꯅ ꯂꯥꯏꯅꯤꯡꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯨꯏꯅ ꯂꯦꯞꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫ ꯂꯥꯏ ꯍꯔꯥꯑꯣꯕꯗ ꯀꯨꯏꯅ ꯆꯠꯀꯗꯕ ꯑꯌꯨꯛ ꯑꯗꯨꯗ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯊꯥꯒꯗꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Chana dal soaks four hours. Five hours before the bell in all.
start.l: ꯆꯅꯥ ꯗꯥꯜ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯅꯃꯃꯤ꯫ ꯒꯪ ꯈꯣꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥ꯫

vessel.en: A 40 L vessel with a close lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯆꯦꯛꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯴꯰ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, and before any long walking day.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯨꯏꯅ ꯆꯠꯀꯗꯕ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Manipuri Masala
recipes.sub: The house blend, bay and coriander led
recipes.sub_l: ꯇꯦꯖꯄꯥꯠ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯣꯛꯆꯥꯎꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ

method.en: This blend is bay-led, which is what distinguishes a Manipuri masala from a plains garam masala. Three hundred grams of bay in two and a half kilos is not a mistake.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯤ ꯇꯦꯖꯄꯥꯠꯅ ꯆꯥꯎꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯁꯤꯅ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯕꯨ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯅ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ꯫

method.en: There is no nutmeg and no mace here. The valley blend is lighter than a Punjabi one and adding them makes it something else.
method.l: ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯖꯥꯏꯐꯜ ꯌꯥꯑꯣꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Spread the whole spices in the sun for half a day. Moisture left in them clogs the grinder and shortens the life of the blend.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯊꯝꯗꯨꯅ ꯀꯪꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Roast each spice separately on a dry pan on a low flame. They are different sizes and roasting them together burns the small ones.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯇꯣꯉꯥꯅ ꯀꯥꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Take each off the moment it smells, not when it changes colour. Colour is a late signal.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯝ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯔꯛꯄ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cool completely, grind in small batches, sieve, and store in glass away from the stove.
method.l: ꯏꯡꯍꯅꯂꯒ ꯁꯨꯝꯂꯒ ꯀꯥꯆꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Bay-led and light. Roasting each spice separately is the whole difference between a house blend and a bought one.
recipes.why_l: ꯇꯦꯖꯄꯥꯠꯅ ꯆꯥꯎꯕ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯆꯥꯅ ꯂꯩꯕ꯫

start.en: Sun the whole spices half a day. Grind in one sitting.
start.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A heavy pan and a dry grinder. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯀꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯟꯗꯔ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Made twice a year.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯑꯅꯤꯔꯛ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Umorok Powder
recipes.sub: Dried and ground king chilli
recipes.sub_l: ꯀꯪꯂꯕ ꯎꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯁꯨꯝꯂꯕ

method.en: Grind this outdoors and never in a closed kitchen. The airborne dust from umorok will empty a room and it genuinely hurts to breathe.
method.l: ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯗ ꯁꯨꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫

method.en: Wear cloth over the nose and mouth and gloves on the hands, and wash the grinder outside afterwards.
method.l: ꯃꯥꯏꯗ ꯐꯤ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯈꯨꯠꯇ ꯐꯤ ꯌꯦꯠꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Dry the chillies whole in full sun for a week until they rattle when shaken.
method.l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯃ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯀꯪꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Do not dry them over a fire. Smoke-dried umorok tastes of the fire rather than of the chilli, which is right for a metpa and wrong for a powder.
method.l: ꯃꯩꯗ ꯀꯪꯍꯅꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Grind in short bursts, letting the dust settle between each, and open the lid away from the face.
method.l: ꯈꯔꯈꯔ ꯁꯨꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯃꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯄꯅ ꯍꯥꯡꯗꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: One kilo is more than a temple kitchen will use in a year. Label the jar clearly and keep it separate from ordinary chilli powder.
method.l: ꯀꯦꯖꯤ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃ ꯆꯠꯀꯅꯤ꯫ ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯃꯃꯤꯡ ꯏꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: A year's supply from four kilos, and the only recipe in these books that needs a mask.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦꯖꯤ ꯴ ꯅ ꯆꯍꯤ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯡꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Sun-dry the chillies a full week. Grind outdoors, wearing cloth over the face.
start.l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯃ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯀꯪꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: Drying trays and a dry grinder. One cook, gloved and masked.
vessel.l: ꯒ꯭ꯔꯥꯏꯟꯗꯔ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ, ꯐꯤꯅ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯗꯨꯅ꯫

season.en: Made in October when the chillies ripen.
season.l: ꯑꯣꯛꯇꯣꯕꯔꯗ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Perilla Powder
recipes.sub: Roasted ground perilla seed
recipes.sub_l: ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯟꯗꯣꯛ ꯁꯨꯝꯂꯕ

method.en: There is one ingredient on this page and that is the point. Perilla is what thickens a Manipuri pot where a plains kitchen would use cream or cashew.
method.l: ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯄꯣꯠꯆꯩ ꯑꯃ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Roast in lots of no more than half a kilo. A full pan roasts unevenly and one scorched patch makes the whole grinding bitter.
method.l: ꯀꯦꯖꯤ ꯑꯗꯣꯝ ꯑꯗꯣꯝ ꯀꯥꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Keep the flame at its lowest and move the seed constantly with a flat ladle.
method.l: ꯃꯩ ꯃꯆꯥꯗ ꯊꯝꯂꯒ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛꯇ ꯍꯨꯡꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Take it off the moment it begins to pop. Perilla goes from roasted to burnt in about twenty seconds — the shortest window of any spice in these books.
method.l: ꯄꯨꯡꯂꯛꯄ ꯃꯇꯃꯗ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟꯗ ꯲꯰ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cool completely on a tray before grinding. Warm seed releases its oil and grinds to a sticky paste that will not keep.
method.l: ꯁꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯥꯡꯗ ꯏꯡꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Grind coarse and make small quantities. Perilla is high in oil and turns rancid within six weeks.
method.l: ꯑꯔꯨꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯁꯨꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ, ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯶ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯆꯠꯀꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: One ingredient, twenty seconds of judgement, and it is in a third of the recipes in this book.
recipes.why_l: ꯄꯣꯠꯆꯩ ꯑꯃ, ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟꯗ ꯲꯰ ꯒꯤ ꯋꯥꯐꯝ꯫

start.en: Roast in small lots and cool completely. Grind the same day.
start.l: ꯈꯔꯈꯔ ꯀꯥꯡꯂꯒ ꯏꯡꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A heavy pan and a stone grinder. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯀꯔꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯁꯨꯝꯕꯜ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Made in November after the harvest.
season.l: ꯅꯕꯦꯝꯕꯔꯗ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ꯫

recipes.name: Thoiding Machu
recipes.sub: Dry chilli ground alone, the only heat a Manipuri kitchen keeps
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯊꯃꯖꯕ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯅꯤ — ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯁꯨꯃꯂꯕ

method.en: Sun the chilli two days before it is ground. A chilli with any damp in it clogs the mill and the powder cakes in the tin within a week.
method.l: ꯁꯨꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯅꯕ ꯃꯁꯤꯟ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯤꯡꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥꯗ ꯀꯅꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Take the stalks off and keep the seeds in. The seed is where the heat is and a seedless thoiding machu is a colouring and nothing more.
method.l: ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨꯗꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯂꯩꯇꯕ ꯊꯣꯏꯗꯤꯡ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯄꯤꯕ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ, ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫

method.en: Grind it coarse and never to a dust. A dust burns in the first second of a tempering; a coarse powder gives the kitchen eight seconds to work in.
method.l: ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ, ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠꯀꯨꯝꯅ ꯀꯩꯗꯧꯉꯩꯗꯁꯨ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠꯅ ꯐꯣꯗꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯑꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟꯗꯗꯃꯛ ꯆꯥꯛꯏ; ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯗ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟꯗ ꯅꯤꯄꯥꯜ ꯄꯤ꯫

method.en: Grind in the open and not in the kitchen. Three kilos of chilli in a mill clears a closed room of everyone in it inside a minute.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯗ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯗ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯍꯨꯃꯅ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯂꯣꯅꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯀꯥ ꯑꯃꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯤ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Four hundred rupees a kilo and it lasts a Manipuri kitchen four months. There is no garam masala in a Meitei dish; this powder and the perilla are the whole spice shelf.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯴꯰꯰, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯊꯥ ꯃꯔꯤ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫ ꯃꯩꯇꯩꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯇ ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ; ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯒꯤ ꯐꯂꯤ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯟꯗꯣꯛꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Two days in the sun before grinding. Thirty minutes at the mill.
start.l: ꯁꯨꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯗ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯳꯰꯫

vessel.en: A drying mat, a mill in the open and a tin with a close lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯐꯛ, ꯃꯄꯥꯟꯗ ꯃꯁꯤꯅ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯦꯛꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Ground in Mera when the Ukhrul chilli comes down, used all year.
season.l: ꯎꯈ꯭ꯔꯨꯂꯒꯤ ꯃꯣꯔꯣꯛ ꯂꯥꯛꯄ ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯖꯩ, ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫

recipes.name: Garam Masala
recipes.sub: The warm powder for the north Indian dishes on the same menu
recipes.sub_l: ꯃꯦꯅꯨ ꯑꯗꯨꯃꯛꯇ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯅꯣꯡꯄꯣꯛ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯥꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ

method.en: Roast each spice on its own and not together. A clove is done in forty seconds and a coriander seed takes three minutes; roasted together, half the tin is burnt.
method.l: ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯃꯈꯣꯌ ꯃꯈꯣꯌꯒꯤ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ, ꯄꯨꯟꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯂꯧꯪ ꯑꯃ ꯁꯦꯀꯦꯟꯗ ꯴꯰ꯗ ꯁꯦꯝꯃꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯍꯥꯡꯃ ꯃꯔꯨꯗ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ ꯆꯪꯏ; ꯄꯨꯟꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯆꯥꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Let every spice go completely cold before it is ground. Warm spice in a mill turns to an oily cake and no sieve will take it apart.
method.l: ꯁꯨꯃꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯗ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅ ꯊꯥꯎ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯀꯦꯛ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯠꯇꯅ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯀꯥꯏꯊꯣꯛꯄ ꯉꯃꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Two kilos and no more at a time. Ground garam masala is at its best for six weeks and a bigger tin is smelling of dust by the third month.
method.l: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯅꯤ ꯈꯛꯇ, ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯁꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯇꯔꯨꯛ ꯐꯖꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯍꯨꯃꯁꯨꯕꯗ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠꯀꯤ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯄꯤꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Add it at the end of the cooking and not the start. A garam masala boiled twenty minutes has given up everything it had.
method.l: ꯍꯨꯝꯕꯒꯤ ꯑꯍꯧꯕꯗ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯑꯔꯣꯏꯕꯗ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯜꯂꯨ꯫ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯀꯨꯅ ꯍꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯅ ꯃꯁꯥꯗ ꯂꯩꯔꯤꯕ ꯄꯨꯝꯅꯃꯛ ꯄꯤꯊꯔꯦ꯫

recipes.why: Seventeen hundred rupees a kilo and it lasts six weeks. Half the menu of a Manipuri temple is now north Indian and there is no honest way round keeping this tin.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯱꯷꯰꯰, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯁꯤ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯇꯔꯨꯛ ꯂꯩꯍꯧꯏ꯫ ꯍꯧꯖꯤꯛ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯉ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯦꯅꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏ ꯅꯣꯡꯄꯣꯛ ꯏꯟꯗꯤꯌꯥꯒꯤꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯊꯝꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯅꯥꯅꯊꯣꯛꯅꯕ ꯑꯆꯨꯝꯕ ꯂꯝꯕꯤ ꯑꯃꯠꯇ ꯂꯩꯇꯦ꯫

start.en: Roast, cool completely, grind and sieve. Two hours for two kilos.
start.l: ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯒ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒ ꯁꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯆꯥꯅꯨ꯫ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯅꯤꯒꯤ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A dry pan, a cooling tray, a mill and a tin with a close lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ, ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯇ꯭ꯔꯦ, ꯃꯁꯤꯅ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯦꯛꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Ground every six weeks, all year.
season.l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯇꯔꯨꯛ ꯇꯔꯨꯛꯀꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯖꯩ, ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Chakhao Machu
recipes.sub: Black rice roasted and milled for the kheer and the laddu
recipes.sub_l: ꯈꯤꯔ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯂꯗ꯭ꯗꯨꯒꯤꯗꯃꯛ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗꯨꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯃꯨꯕ

method.en: Wash it once and dry it a full day in the sun before roasting. Chakhao holds water in the bran and a damp grain will not roast evenly.
method.l: ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯇꯪ ꯍꯥꯝꯗꯣꯛꯂꯒ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯃꯄꯨꯡ ꯐꯥꯅ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯨ꯫ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎꯅ ꯃꯍꯨꯃꯗ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯊꯃꯖꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯃꯔꯨꯅ ꯃꯥꯟꯅꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Roast it dry until the kitchen smells of it and no longer. Chakhao past that point goes bitter and four kilos of it is not cheap enough to throw.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯗ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯃꯗꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯔꯤ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯪꯊꯣꯛꯅꯕ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Mill it coarse, to the grain of a semolina. A fine chakhao flour gives a kheer the texture of paint and the colour is all that is left of it.
method.l: ꯁꯨꯖꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯥꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯈꯤꯔꯗ ꯔꯪꯒꯤ ꯃꯑꯣꯡ ꯄꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯋꯥꯠꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Keep it in a tin and not a jar in the light. Chakhao loses its purple to sunlight and a pale kheer is not what the hall came for.
method.l: ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯐꯃꯗ ꯖꯥꯔ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥꯗ ꯊꯝꯃꯨ꯫ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯀꯤ ꯃꯉꯥꯂꯗ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎꯅ ꯃꯁꯤꯒꯤ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯃꯥꯡꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯍꯥꯅꯕ ꯈꯤꯔ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯨꯞꯄꯨꯅ ꯄꯥꯃꯖꯕ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫

recipes.why: Two hundred and seventy rupees a kilo and it saves the kitchen milling a kilo at a time. Bishnupur chakhao is a Manipur crop and a temple that buys it keeps a Loktak field planted.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯷꯰, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃ ꯁꯨꯃꯕꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯀꯅꯕꯤ꯫ ꯕꯤꯁ꯭ꯅꯨꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯂꯧꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯩꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯉ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯂꯣꯛꯇꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯂꯧ ꯑꯃ ꯊꯥꯅ ꯊꯝꯃꯤ꯫

start.en: A day in the sun, then roast and mill. Two hours at the mill.
start.l: ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠ ꯑꯃ ꯅꯨꯃꯤꯠꯇ, ꯑꯗꯨꯒ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗꯨꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯗ ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A drying mat, a dry pan and a tin that keeps the light out. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯐꯛ, ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯉꯥꯜ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: Milled in Mera after the harvest, used all year.
season.l: ꯂꯧ ꯂꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯦꯔꯥꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯖꯩ, ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯩ꯫

recipes.name: Phou Machu
recipes.sub: Plain rice roasted and milled, the thickener for every thongba
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ — ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗꯨꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ

method.en: Roast it until it just takes colour, no further. Rice roasted brown thickens as well but every thongba it goes into tastes of toast.
method.l: ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯃ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯈꯛꯇ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ, ꯃꯗꯨꯗꯒꯤ ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯑꯍꯨꯝꯕ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯐꯥꯑꯣꯕ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯅꯁꯨ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯗꯨꯕꯨ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯆꯪꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯃꯛꯇ ꯆꯥꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯍꯥꯎ ꯄꯤ꯫

method.en: Mill it coarse. A fine flour goes to lumps the second it touches a hot thongba and the lumps do not break up again.
method.l: ꯑꯆꯧꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯑꯔꯦꯞꯄ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯁꯥꯕ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯗ ꯁꯣꯛꯄ ꯃꯇꯃꯗꯃꯛ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯟꯅ ꯀꯥꯏꯗꯦ꯫

method.en: Mix it to a slurry in cold water before it goes into the vessel. Thrown in dry, five kilos of it becomes five hundred lumps.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯐꯨꯗ ꯆꯪꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩꯗ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯕ ꯏꯁꯤꯡꯗ ꯌꯦꯡꯁꯤꯜꯂꯨ꯫ ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯍꯨꯟꯗꯣꯛꯂꯕꯗꯤ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯃꯉꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯃꯉꯥꯔꯥ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

method.en: Keep it dry and use it in a month. Roasted rice flour picks up the damp of an Imphal Kalen and goes musty in the tin.
method.l: ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯊꯝꯂꯒ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯨ꯫ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯃꯆꯨꯅ ꯏꯝꯐꯥꯂꯒꯤ ꯀꯥꯂꯦꯅꯒꯤ ꯑꯍꯥꯡꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯁꯤꯜꯂꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥꯗ ꯃꯅꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯛꯏ꯫

recipes.why: Seventy-six rupees a kilo, the cheapest thing on this shelf, and it is what lets a Manipuri kitchen thicken thirty litres of thongba with no besan and no cream.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯷꯶ — ꯐꯂꯤ ꯑꯁꯤꯗ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯃꯜ ꯇꯝꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯑꯗꯨ; ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯕꯦꯁꯟ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯀ꯭ꯔꯤꯝ ꯌꯥꯑꯣꯗꯅ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡꯅ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ ꯂꯤꯇꯔ ꯳꯰ ꯑꯔꯨꯝꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯕ ꯉꯃꯍꯜꯂꯤꯕ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯁꯤꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Roast and mill in one hour. Made every month.
start.l: ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗꯨꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯊꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯁꯥꯏ꯫

vessel.en: A dry pan, a mill and a tin with a close lid. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ, ꯃꯁꯤꯅ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯦꯛꯁꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯆꯦꯠ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, and milled fresh every month.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯥ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ ꯑꯅꯧꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯖꯩ꯫

recipes.name: Dhaniya Machu
recipes.sub: Coriander seed roasted and milled alone, a tin every fortnight
recipes.sub_l: ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯑꯅꯤꯗ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ ꯑꯃ — ꯃꯁꯥꯅ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯗꯨꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯂꯕ ꯍꯥꯡꯃ ꯃꯔꯨ

method.en: Roast it on the lowest flame you can hold. Coriander burns from the inside and a seed that looks right can already be bitter.
method.l: ꯄꯥꯏꯕ ꯉꯃꯕ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯅꯦꯃꯕ ꯃꯩꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯨ꯫ ꯍꯥꯡꯃ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯃꯅꯨꯡꯗꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯛꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯤꯠꯅ ꯌꯦꯡꯕꯗ ꯆꯨꯃꯗꯨꯅ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯃꯔꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨ ꯑꯀꯍꯕ ꯑꯣꯏꯔꯝꯕ ꯌꯥꯏ꯫

method.en: Ground alone and not in a garam masala. Three quarters of the coriander a temple kitchen uses goes into dishes that want no clove in them.
method.l: ꯒꯔꯝ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥꯗ ꯅꯠꯇꯅ ꯃꯁꯥꯅ ꯁꯨꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫ ꯂꯥꯏꯁꯉꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯍꯥꯡꯃ ꯃꯔꯨꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯤꯁꯨꯕ ꯑꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯂꯧꯪ ꯆꯪꯗꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯇ ꯆꯪꯏ꯫

method.en: Mill it medium and sieve it once. The husk that comes off in the sieve is what floats on a thongba and looks like dust on the surface.
method.l: ꯃꯔꯤꯜꯃꯔꯤꯜꯂꯕ ꯃꯑꯣꯡꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯂꯒ ꯑꯃꯨꯛꯇꯪ ꯆꯥꯅꯨ꯫ ꯆꯥꯅꯤꯗ ꯂꯧꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯍꯨꯝ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯊꯣꯡꯕꯒꯤ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯄꯣꯝꯏ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯃꯊꯛꯇ ꯅꯨꯡꯁꯤꯠꯀꯨꯝꯅ ꯎꯏ꯫

method.en: Three kilos at a time and no more. A dhaniya machu is at its best for a fortnight and after a month it is a filler.
method.l: ꯃꯇꯝ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯍꯨꯝ ꯈꯛꯇ, ꯍꯦꯟꯅ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫ ꯗꯅꯤꯌꯥ ꯃꯆꯨ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯐꯖꯩ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯊꯥ ꯑꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯃꯗꯨ ꯍꯥꯄꯆꯤꯅꯕ ꯄꯣꯠ ꯈꯛꯇꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: Two hundred and forty rupees a kilo. Coriander is the one spice a Manipuri kitchen uses by the kilo rather than the gram, and milling it in the house is half the price of the packet.
recipes.why_l: ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ. ꯑꯃꯗ ꯂꯨꯄ꯭ꯄꯥ ꯲꯴꯰꯫ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯀꯁꯥꯡ ꯑꯃꯅ ꯒ꯭ꯔꯥꯃꯒꯤ ꯃꯍꯨꯠꯇ ꯀꯦ.ꯖꯤ.ꯅ ꯁꯤꯖꯤꯟꯅꯕ ꯃꯁꯥꯂꯥ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯥꯡꯃ ꯃꯔꯨꯅꯤ, ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯌꯨꯃꯗ ꯁꯨꯃꯕꯅ ꯄꯦꯀꯦꯠꯀꯤ ꯃꯃꯂꯒꯤ ꯃꯈꯥꯏꯅꯤ꯫

start.en: Roast, cool and mill in one hour. Made every fortnight.
start.l: ꯄꯨꯡ ꯑꯃꯗ ꯊꯥꯡꯒꯂꯒ ꯑꯗꯨꯝ ꯑꯣꯏꯍꯅꯒ ꯁꯨꯃꯨ꯫ ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯑꯅꯤꯗ ꯁꯥꯏ꯫

vessel.en: A dry pan, a mill, a sieve and a tin. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯑꯀꯪꯕ ꯀꯗꯥꯏ, ꯃꯁꯤꯅ, ꯆꯥꯅꯤ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯗꯕ꯭ꯕꯥ꯫ ꯃꯤꯑꯣꯏ ꯑꯃ꯫

season.en: All year, every fortnight.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯆꯌꯣꯜ ꯑꯅꯤ ꯑꯅꯤꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Plain Rice
recipes.sub: Valley rice, boiled and drained
recipes.sub_l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯊꯣꯡꯕ

method.en: The valley eats a short, slightly sticky rice, not a basmati. Do not buy basmati for this book — it is wrong on the plate and costs three times as much.
method.l: ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯗ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯄꯤꯀꯄ ꯆꯥꯏ, ꯕꯥꯁꯃꯇꯤ ꯅꯠꯇꯦ꯫

method.en: Rinse until the water runs clear and soak twenty minutes.
method.l: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯁꯦꯡꯗ꯭ꯔꯤꯉꯩ ꯆꯦꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Boil in an open vessel with plenty of water and drain the excess off. This is the drained method and it is what the valley uses.
method.l: ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯌꯥꯝꯅ ꯍꯥꯞꯂꯒ ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯒ ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯀꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Keep the rice water. It is drunk warm with salt, given to anyone unwell, and thrown away only by a wasteful kitchen.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯀꯤ ꯏꯁꯤꯡ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Cover and rest ten minutes after draining.
method.l: ꯄꯤꯛꯊꯣꯛꯂꯕ ꯃꯇꯨꯡꯗ ꯀꯨꯞꯁꯤꯅꯗꯨꯅ ꯱꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯊꯝꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

method.en: Do not fork it through. The grains are meant to sit together and the broth of a kangshoi is poured over them.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛ ꯑꯗꯨ ꯍꯨꯡꯂꯣꯏꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

recipes.why: The base of every meal in this book. Buying the right rice matters more than anything done to it afterwards.
recipes.why_l: ꯑꯆꯨꯝꯕ ꯆꯥꯛ ꯂꯩꯕ ꯑꯗꯨꯅ ꯈ꯭ꯋꯥꯏꯗꯒꯤ ꯃꯔꯨꯑꯣꯏ꯫

start.en: Rinse and soak twenty minutes. Start forty minutes before serving.
start.l: ꯆꯦꯛꯂꯒ ꯲꯰ ꯃꯤꯅꯤꯠ ꯅꯃꯒꯗꯕꯅꯤ꯫

vessel.en: A heavy 45 L vessel and a large strainer. One cook.
vessel.l: ꯴꯵ ꯂꯤ.ꯒꯤ ꯆꯥꯐꯨ ꯑꯃꯁꯨꯡ ꯆꯥꯅꯤ꯫

season.en: All year, at every meal.
season.l: ꯆꯍꯤ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ, ꯆꯥꯛ ꯈꯨꯗꯤꯡꯗ꯫

recipes.name: Chak-hao Amubi
recipes.sub: Steamed black rice
recipes.sub_l: ꯊꯣꯡꯂꯕ ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ

method.en: Chak-hao is the black rice of the valley and it has a Geographical Indication of its own. It grows nowhere else in India in this quantity.
method.l: ꯆꯥꯛꯍꯥꯎ ꯑꯁꯤ ꯃꯅꯤꯄꯨꯔꯒꯤꯅꯤ, ꯃꯐꯝ ꯑꯇꯣꯞꯄꯗ ꯐꯪꯗꯦ꯫
